newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Tuesday was quiet for the second consecutive day as packers and cattle owners continued their standoff, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids at $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $64.00 to $65.00, they said. The bids were unchanged from last week's late sales and top price of $62.00.
Fed prices were seen supported this week by outlooks for lighter cattle supplies starting the next few weeks and extending into the fall, several cattle feeders said.
Feedlots have been able to remain current this summer as large numbers of cattle placed on feed during the spring became market ready.
If the feedlots can remain current until supplies start coming back down, then the potential for higher prices will grow, sources said.
Prospects for firm fed cattle prices were reinforced by recent strength in CME live cattle futures and ideas that beef prices were near a bottom and ready to rebound, they said.
Beef prices at midday Tuesday were quoted up $0.03 to $0.49 per cwt on 173 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said.
